La prohibición de dividir entre cero cos: The ban on dividing by zero took a long time to settle. The Indian mathematician Brahmagupta, in the year 628, was the first to treat zero as a number in its own right, but he went wrong on exactly this point: he wrote that zero divided by zero is zero. Five hundred years later, Bhaskara proposed that dividing by zero gave infinity, which does not work either. It took the rigour of the nineteenth century to accept the correct answer, which is humbler: that operation is simply not defined.

Los valores prohibidos son la causa de u: Forbidden values are the cause of a good share of software failures. When an application closes by itself or shows an incomprehensible error, very often something has ended up dividing by zero: an average worked out over an empty list, a percentage of a total that turned out to be nil. Working out in advance which values break an expression is exactly what a careful programmer does before shipping.

Merece la pena entender <em>por qué</em>: It is worth understanding why, because anyone who understands it stops making the mistake. Reducing a fraction is dividing top and bottom by the same thing, and to be able to divide the whole numerator by something, that something has to be multiplying all of the numerator. A factor multiplies the whole; a summand is only a part.
